late_approval.question: Does a client that connects after an approval request opened receive that open request?
late_approval.runner: starts codex --no-daemon app-server --listen unix://<scratch>/app.sock through codex_router.command and child_environment in a scratch CODEX_HOME, then runs python -m scripts.codex_app_server_probe <sock> <repo> late_approval <out>
late_approval.finding: A late connection that only calls thread/read receives no approval request and no turn events. A late connection that calls thread/resume receives the open request with the same id, after the resume reply and before the reply to its next thread/read, and later sees its resolution. Both bearer accounts.
late_approval.decision: The pump starts with thread/resume then thread/read, so an open approval is recorded before its first step. The hold on a turn already running at connect is dropped: such a turn is steered like any observed turn, and an open approval still holds delivery.

observations: With the pre-connect hold, a Codex worker whose opening turn never ended received no push delivery and pulled its mail through msg inbox; the hold is dropped in this pull request.
Swarm restore does not restore the receipts journal; item states are restored and the swarm resumes paused awaiting decision.
A launch viewer outlived retire once and was closed by its pid (raw/a-retire-after.txt).
Several replacement launches failed with the harness did not report its route within 30s, which stretched the socket loss recovery to about 270 s.
A proof swarm over a real checkout filed promotion fixer tasks and its ci agent opened a real pull request; promotion_watch now skips proof swarms.
accounts_note: The fleets ran on the personal bearer account; the business bearer account was qualified by the late approval probe only and was at its week quota warning during the run.
